A local group on a Windows host, and who is in it. Settings left unset are left as they are.

Use `windows_group` to keep a local group on a Windows host and make sure the right accounts are in it. Members are compared by SID, so `LAB\alice` and `lab\Alice` are the same account.

## Example usage

```hcl
step "app_admins" {
  windows_group {
    name        = "AppAdmins"
    description = "Can manage the app"
    members     = ["appsvc", "LAB\\alice"]
  }
}
```

```hcl
step "rdp_only_ops" {
  windows_group {
    name          = "Remote Desktop Users"
    members       = ["LAB\\ops"]
    authoritative = true
  }
}
```

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `authoritative` | bool | No | true makes members the complete list: anyone else is taken out. Never the login Conn3x uses. |
| `description` | string | No | Description, up to 48 characters. |
| `members` | set of string | No | Users and groups that must be in it, by name, such as LAB\alice, or by SID. Others are left in unless authoritative is set. |
| `name` | string | Yes | Group name, such as Remote Desktop Users. |
| `on_remove` | string | No | What happens on the host when this resource is removed: "forget" (default) leaves the group, "delete" deletes it. |

## Read-only attributes

Conn3x sets these; reference them as `conn3x_windows_group.<circuit>__<step>["<host>"].<name>`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_sync` | bool | Whether the group matched at the last refresh. |
| `revision` | string | Changes each time Conn3x changes this on the host. Handlers watch it. |

A step lowers to the `conn3x_windows_group` resource, one instance per host, and connects with its circuit's `ssh` block.

## How it works

**Members.** By default, `members` are added and nobody else is taken out. With `authoritative = true` the list is complete: anyone else is removed on apply. In a group the login Conn3x uses belongs to, such as `Administrators`, Conn3x refuses to remove the login or any group it gets its rights through, such as `Domain Admins`, so apply fails until the list keeps them.

A member that doesn't exist yet, such as a user a later step makes, shows the group as out of sync rather than failing the plan. At apply, a name that still doesn't resolve is an error.

## Removal

By default, deleting a `windows_group` step leaves the group and its members. With `on_remove = "delete"` it deletes the group.
